title: Spotlight on IC 3583
caption: The irregular galaxy IC 3583, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: IC 3583 · constellation Virgo · about 30 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This delicate blue group of stars is an irregular galaxy called IC 3583, some 30 million light-years away in the constellation Virgo (The Virgin). It seems to have no clear structure, but astronomers have found a bar of stars running through its center.

A bar is a straight band of stars that crosses a galaxy's center. Bars like this are common in the Universe. They appear in most spiral galaxies, in many irregular galaxies and in some lenticular galaxies, which sit between spirals and ellipticals.

Two of our closest neighbors, the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds, also have bars. That hints that they may once have been barred spiral galaxies that were disrupted or pulled apart by the gravity of the Milky Way. The Magellanic Clouds are small galaxies that orbit the Milky Way.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.32 x 3.28 arcminutes) and distance (30 million light years), the frame spans roughly 29,000 × 29,000 light-years. Its light set out about 30 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys observed IC 3583 in visible and near-infrared light. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Part of this light is near-infrared, which the eye cannot see, and the galaxy is far too faint to see without a telescope.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys recorded IC 3583 through visible and near-infrared filters. The picture was released as an ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week. Lenticular galaxies have a central bulge and a disc but no clear spiral arms.
alt: A loose, delicate group of blue stars forming an irregular galaxy.
